sentiment.rationale: Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance from 'more than $13.5 billion' (previously stated as 'more than $13.5 billion' but now explicitly raised from prior expectations) and raised operating pretax margin expansion guidance from 'about a half a point' to 'about a point'. Revenue guidance was reaffirmed at 'at least 5 percent' constant currency growth, but the strong first-half performance and raised profitability and cash flow guidance represent a meaningful upward revision to forward expectations. The guidance raise is organic, attributed to business performance and productivity initiatives, not primarily to FX or one-time items.

summary.revenue: $17.0 billion, up 8 percent (5 percent at constant currency).
summary.eps: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations of $2.31, up 18% year-over-year; Operating (Non-GAAP) diluted EPS of $2.80, up 15% year-over-year.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025: constant currency revenue growth of at least 5 percent; free cash flow now expected to exceed $13.5 billion (raised); operating pretax margin expansion of about a point (raised from about half a point); software revenue growth approaching double digits; Red Hat mid-teens growth; infrastructure contributing about 1.5 points to IBM's revenue growth; consulting growth contribution prudently cautious; Q3 2025 comfortable with consensus estimates for revenue and profitability.
summary.margin: GAAP Gross Profit Margin: 58.8%, up 200 basis points; Operating (Non-GAAP) Gross Profit Margin: 60.1%, up 230 basis points. GAAP Pre-tax Income Margin: 15.3%, up 120 basis points; Operating (Non-GAAP) Pre-tax Income Margin: 18.8%, up 110 basis points.
key_risks: Geopolitical tensions prompting a few clients to move cautiously.
US federal spending somewhat constrained in the first half.
Consulting revenue flat, impacted by dynamic demand environment and clients prioritizing cost-efficient high-impact investments.
Delayed decision-making, especially in discretionary projects, impacting consulting signings.
Transaction processing revenue declined 2% as clients prioritized hardware spend at the beginning of a new z17 cycle.
Distributed infrastructure revenue down 17% with product cycle dynamics impacting power.
Global trade dynamics requiring prudent protection of supply chain.
Foregone interest income from HashiCorp acquisition as a headwind to free cash flow.
key_opportunities: Generative AI book of business now over $7.5 billion, accelerating quarter over quarter.
Red Hat growth accelerated to 14%, with OpenShift revenue growing over 20% and ARR at $1.7 billion.
HashiCorp integration off to a strong start, accelerating bookings growth and pipeline 3x last year.
Strong z17 launch with over 100% MIPS capacity shipped, driving long-term multiplier effect.
Productivity initiatives targeting $4.5 billion in annual run rate savings by end of 2025.
Software mix shift to about 45% of business, with ARR growing 10%.
New AI product advancements: Watson x Orchestra with 150+ domain-specific agents, z17 with Telen two processor enabling 450 billion AI inference operations per day.
Expanding partner ecosystem with Oracle, AWS, Salesforce, Microsoft, etc.
Optimism around macro environment, with strength in Japan, South Asia, Middle East, and resilient Europe.
Federal government focus shifting to modernization and AI, with direct engagement at highest levels.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management repeatedly uses phrases like 'we feel even more confident about the year of approaching double digits' (Jim Kavanaugh) and 'I would now turn my way all the way to optimism around the macro environment' (Arvind Krishna), and raised guidance on free cash flow and operating margin.
